root_motivation: An agent's chain passed host.tool_test's dry run and then failed its first real call on a mapping the dry run had already flagged as unresolved, nested as data (host_tool_test reported {rows: {unresolved_path: "$.prev.rows"}}, then host_tool_call failed `mapping path '$.prev.rows' resolved to nothing`); a second agent's python tool failed its dry run on "composition is unavailable" and then succeeded on the real call. Both trace to one root cause: host.tool_test can only say "I couldn't resolve this", never "this will definitely fail" or "I cannot check this here, call it instead" -- an agent cannot tell a benign gap in the dry run's own knowledge apart from a spec that is actually broken, so it learns to distrust try_before_call. This PRD gives host.tool_test (and host.tool_publish's dry_run gate) a verdict (pass, will_fail, unverifiable) with the evidence needed to fix the spec before it ever calls.
user_persona: An agent building a chain who reads host.tool_test before calling and needs to know whether a $.prev/$.steps[i] mapping is provably wrong, provably fine, or unknowable from a dry run; an agent publishing a composing python tool, who needs to know its dry run's silence about composition is the dry run's own limitation, not a broken tool; Operator Joe, who wants will_fail verdicts per day as specs fixed before a failed real call.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a chain whose step 2 maps rows: "$.prev.rows" and whose step 1 tool declares outputs result, count, When host.tool_test runs, Then verdict: will_fail with one failure {step: 2, path: "$.prev.rows", predecessor_keys: ["result", "count"]} and no step executed.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/testtruth_ac01_chain_prev_will_fail.rs -- publishes an http step1 declaring outputs ["result","count"] and an echo step2 mapping rows: "$.prev.rows", calls host.tool_test, and asserts verdict/failures/steps:[] exactly. kinds::chain::verdict (a new static, call-args-independent engine shared with host.tool_publish's gate) checks the FIRST segment after $.prev/$.steps[i] against the predecessor's Kind::declared_outputs names; handler::tool_test computes it before kind.call ever runs and returns immediately on will_fail, so a chain with an allowlisted host step earlier in the pipeline still executes nothing.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the same chain with step 2 mapped to $.prev.result, When host.tool_test runs, Then verdict: pass and resolved_args carries no unresolved_path.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/testtruth_ac02_chain_prev_result_pass.rs -- same fixture, step2 remapped to "$.prev.result" ("result" is one of step1's declared names), asserts verdict: pass and that resolved_args.rows carries no unresolved_path key. dry_run_report's per-field loop now consults the same static check's per-path pass set (steps_verdict) to suppress the unresolved_path wrapper for a mapping it has confirmed resolves against the predecessor's schema, even though the dry run still has no real value to show without dispatching.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a chain whose step 1 is an http tool with no declared outputs, When step 2 maps $.prev.anything, Then verdict: unverifiable with reason naming step 1 and next pointing at host_tool_call.

No production code change beyond AC1/AC2's engine -- this is its third branch (Kind::declared_outputs returns empty or the tool/kind can't be resolved at all).

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a python tool whose source calls mcphost.call(...), When host.tool_test runs, Then verdict: unverifiable, reason: "composition is not executed in a dry run", next.tool: "host_tool_call", and the error text is under detail; and host.tool_call of the same tool succeeds.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/testtruth_ac04_python_compose_unverifiable_in_dry_run.rs -- publishes a callee and a composer (mcphost.call("callee", ...)) python tool, asserts host.tool_test(composer) succeeds with verdict/reason/next/detail (detail contains "McphostCallError"), then asserts host.tool_call(composer) succeeds and composes normally. PythonKind::call (both the cold path and the warm-reuse path) now matches the sandboxed exception's own stable class name (McphostCallError, from compose_dispatch's `composition is unavailable in this call context`, which fires because host.tool_test's CallCtx always leaves compose_children unset) rather than its free-text message, and turns that one case into a successful verdict:unverifiable value instead of propagating the hard error.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given an echo tool, When host.tool_test runs, Then verdict: pass and the contract test asserts verdict is present on every kind's dry-run response.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/testtruth_ac05_verdict_on_every_kind_dry_run.rs -- one test publishes and dry-runs a bare echo tool (verdict: pass); a second builds a registry with echo+http+chain+python, dry-runs one tool of each kind, and asserts every response carries a verdict key. handler::tool_test now defaults verdict to "pass" (via `.entry(...).or_insert_with`) for any kind that hasn't already set its own (chain's pass/will_fail/unverifiable, or a composing python tool's unverifiable) -- a dry run that got this far ran/resolved cleanly with no composition to doubt. host.tool_test's own wire description now names verdict too (kept under the 160-char cap tests/surface_ac02_dry_run_descriptions.rs enforces); contracts/host-tools.v1.json and docs/tools.md regenerated to match.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given host.tool_publish dry_run=true with the failing chain of AC1, When it runs, Then the gates array carries verdict: will_fail with the same failure and the tool is not published; without dry_run, Then the tool is published and the response carries the advisory verdict.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/testtruth_ac06_publish_gate_verdict.rs -- one test calls host.tool_publish(dry_run:true) with AC1's exact failing chain spec, asserts the gates array's verdict entry (ok: true -- advisory, never blocking) carries will_fail/failures, and that host.tool_test on the name afterward fails (nothing was stored); a second test publishes the identical spec without dry_run, asserts the publish succeeds and the response itself carries verdict/failures. control::tool_publish computes kinds::chain::verdict (the same engine AC1-3 use) right after resolve_steps, pushes a dedicated gate entry after gates_ok is computed (so it can never block a real publish), and merges verdict/failures/reason/next into the real-publish response.

non_goals: Executing real upstream calls inside a dry run -- the dry run stays side-effect free and inside one tenant (PRD's own Non-goals); AC4's fix makes a composing tool's dry run succeed with an honest unverifiable verdict, it never makes mcphost.call actually dispatch under host.tool_test.

Changing the chain mapping grammar -- $.input, $.prev, $.steps[i] stand, and the real call-time resolution (chain.rs:642's own $.prev.result.payload.<field> convention) is unchanged; the static verdict check is a deliberately shallower, schema-level heuristic over just the first segment after $.prev/$.steps[i] (Technical considerations), not a second mapping-resolution engine.

AC8 (the live, post-deploy truth-tier nightly observation that no session records a resolved-to-nothing call failure after a verdict:pass dry run of the same spec) -- operator-provisioned, deferred; not in this dispatch's assigned AC list (AC1-7). AC1-6 already prove the mechanism (the verdict computation and its wiring into both host.tool_test and host.tool_publish) end-to-end against an in-process server.

Blocking publish behind a force flag for a will_fail chain -- the PRD's own Open question defaults to advisory; AC6 implements exactly that (a will_fail chain still publishes, the verdict is visible, never blocking).

host_tool_usage recording dry_run_verdict for operator per-day counting (P2, Requirement 6) -- not an AC in this dispatch's assigned list; the verdict itself (P0/P1, AC1-7) is the prerequisite that P2 would read from, not yet wired to a usage counter.

additional.first_segment_after_prev_checked_against: Requirement 2's own words ("a path whose first segment after the step reference is absent from that schema is will_fail") are read literally: the static check looks at the segment immediately after $.prev/$.steps[i] (e.g. "rows" in $.prev.rows, "result" in $.prev.result) and checks it against the predecessor's Kind::declared_outputs names -- NOT the real runtime wrapper shape ($.prev.result.payload.<field>, chain.rs:279-296/642) a successful call actually needs. AC1's fixture (predecessor declares ["result","count"]; $.prev.rows fails, $.prev.result passes) only makes sense under this reading, since under the real wrapper shape ANY first segment other than literally "result" would always fail structurally regardless of declared outputs, making predecessor_keys meaningless. This is a deliberately shallow, schema-level heuristic (Technical considerations: "kinds without an output schema ... yield unverifiable, never a false will_fail"), not a second implementation of the real mapping grammar (Non-goals: grammar unchanged).
additional.compose_db_compose_kinds_populated_in_to: The static check needs a predecessor's tool row/kind (db.get_tool + kinds.get) to read Kind::declared_outputs, which host.tool_test's CallCtx did not previously carry (compose_db/compose_kinds were both None there, by design, since chain's own dry run never dispatches a step). Populating them is safe because kinds::compose_dispatch checks ctx.compose_children (still left None under host.tool_test) BEFORE it ever reaches compose_db/compose_kinds -- so a composing python tool's mcphost.call still refuses with exactly the same `composition is unavailable in this call context` it always has; only chain's own lookup-only use of the two fields changes.
additional.mcphost_call_error_matched_by_stable_exc: Technical considerations: "matched by a stable error code from the python module, not by substring, so a wording change cannot regress the verdict." PythonKind's own exception-to-KindError mapping (map_envelope_error) already carries data.exception_class = type(e).__name__ verbatim from the sandbox; AC4's detection (composition_unverifiable_detail) matches on exception_class == "McphostCallError" plus code == "tool_exception", never on the message text, even though today's only reachable path to it under host.tool_test happens to produce one specific message.
additional.will_fail_gate_always_ok_true_never_bloc: The PRD's own Open question ("stay advisory") is the only answered one, with 'advisory' as the explicit default. The verdict gate control::tool_publish pushes is therefore ALWAYS {"ok": true, ...} regardless of the computed verdict, and is pushed AFTER gates_ok is computed from the other (secrets/env/network/deps) gates -- a will_fail chain publishes exactly as it would have before this PRD, just with the evidence now visible in the response.
additional.kindexample_blurb_is_not_currently_wired: AC7's own text ("the blurb names the verdict field") is checked directly against ChainKind.example().blurb at the Rust level, not over host.quickstart's RPC response -- grep confirmed KindExample.blurb is read only by src/kinds/docs.rs (the echo/http/python/wasm doc-file-derived blurb, for README rendering) and by nothing in control.rs/handler.rs for ANY kind, chain included; quickstart's response only ever forwards example.spec/example.call_args. Wiring blurb into quickstart's wire response for every kind was out of this PRD's own scope (not named in Requirements/Technical considerations), so AC7's spec-mapping half is proven over the real RPC (quickstart's steps[0].arguments.spec, which chainhost_ac05 already proves flows through verbatim) and its blurb half is proven against the same KindExample struct quickstart builds that spec from.

five_whys_trace.q: Why would a verdict field on host.tool_test actually prevent the kind of failure the grounding incident describes?
five_whys_trace.a: The incident's own turn 23/24 pair shows the gap exactly: host_tool_test already reported {rows: {unresolved_path: "$.prev.rows"}}, which IS the evidence a will_fail verdict needs -- the agent read it and called anyway, because `unresolved_path` alone doesn't say whether that's a benign dry-run limitation or a doomed mapping. Promoting the exact same evidence into an explicit pass/will_fail/unverifiable verdict turns a fact the agent already had, but couldn't interpret, into one it can act on without guessing.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can a dry run tell will_fail from unverifiable at all, when neither case actually runs the predecessor step?
five_whys_trace.a: A predecessor's declared `outputs` (Kind::declared_outputs, already stored at publish time for http/python/wasm specs) is a static fact about what fields that tool's result CAN contain, independent of any particular call's args -- checking a mapping's first segment against that list needs no execution, only a schema it already has on hand. A predecessor with no declared outputs at all (echo, or an http/python spec that didn't declare any) gives the check nothing to compare against, which is exactly what makes THAT case honestly unverifiable rather than a guessed pass or a false will_fail.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a composing python tool need a DIFFERENT verdict path (unverifiable, not will_fail or pass) than a chain's own $.prev mapping?
five_whys_trace.a: A chain step's mapping is checked against a STATIC schema (the predecessor's declared outputs) without ever executing anything; a python tool's mcphost.call has no such schema to consult at all -- the callee could be any tool, and composition itself is categorically unavailable inside host.tool_test's CallCtx (compose_children is never set there, Non-goals: dry run stays side-effect-free and inside one tenant). There is no static fact to check, only an honest 'this dry run cannot see past this point' -- which is unverifiable's whole reason to exist as a THIRD outcome, not a binary pass/fail.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does will_fail need to prevent EVERY step from executing, not just skip the one failing mapping?
five_whys_trace.a: PRD-mcphost-dry-run-side-effects (an earlier PRD) already lets a chain step naming an allowlisted host.* verb actually dispatch during host.tool_test, writing into the same DryRunCtx savepoint. If a will_fail verdict were computed only as the per-step loop reached the failing mapping, an earlier host step in the same chain would already have dispatched by then -- a half-executed 'this will fail' response would contradict the verdict's own claim that calling for real is unsafe. Computing the verdict in a full pre-pass, before the per-step loop ever starts, is what makes 'no step executed' true unconditionally.

five_whys_trace.q: Why extend the SAME verdict engine to host.tool_publish's gate (AC6) rather than leaving the verdict as a host.tool_test-only feature?
five_whys_trace.a: The PRD's own goal is to fix specs BEFORE a failed call, and host.tool_publish is the other place a spec is inspected before anything calls it -- an agent that publishes a will_fail chain and never separately calls host.tool_test on it would otherwise ship exactly the bug this PRD exists to catch. Computing the verdict from the same kinds::chain::verdict function at both sites (rather than two independent implementations) is also the only way the two can never disagree about the same spec.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does the static check replay the real $.prev.result.payload.<field> mapping convention, or something shallower?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Shallower -- only the first segment immediately after $.prev/$.steps[i] is checked against the predecessor's declared output names, matching Requirement 2's own wording and the only reading under which AC1/AC2's fixture (predecessor declares ["result","count"]) makes sense. See hard_constraints.first_segment_after_prev_checked_against_declared_outputs_not_the_real_result_wrapper.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does giving the static check DB/kind access for host.tool_test risk letting a composing python tool's mcphost.call actually dispatch during a dry run?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- compose_db/compose_kinds are populated but compose_children stays unset, and compose_dispatch checks compose_children first, so a composing tool's mcphost.call is refused exactly as before. See hard_constraints.compose_db_compose_kinds_populated_in_tool_test_but_compose_children_stays_unset.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should host.tool_publish's dry_run=true gate ever actually block publish for a will_fail chain?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- the PRD's own Open question defaults to advisory; the gate entry is always ok: true and pushed after gates_ok is computed, so a will_fail chain publishes exactly as before, just with the evidence now visible. See hard_constraints.will_fail_gate_always_ok_true_never_blocks_publish.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Is AC7's blurb assertion checkable over host.quickstart's real RPC response, the way AC7's mapping assertion is?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- KindExample.blurb is not read by quickstart (or by host.tool_publish's description) for any kind, chain included; only docs.rs reads it, for echo/http/python/wasm's doc-file-derived blurb. AC7's blurb half is checked directly against ChainKind.example().blurb instead. See hard_constraints.kindexample_blurb_is_not_currently_wired_into_quickstarts_wire_response.
